Southern Oregon

A quiet place to rest, pray, and begin again.

St Rita's Retreat sits on a hill above the Rogue River Valley — fifteen simple rooms, a chapel, a granite grotto, and trails through the oaks. Come alone, or bring your group.

Check Availability About the Retreat

Welcome

Room to slow down

Some guests arrive with a plan and a schedule. Others arrive with nothing at all. Both are welcome here. Our work is simply to keep the place quiet, the rooms clean, and the days uncluttered, so that whatever brought you up the hill has room to unfold.

Ways to stay

Three kinds of retreat

Personal Retreats

A private room, unhurried days, and the freedom to keep your own rhythm. The chapel, library, lounge, and grounds are open to you throughout your stay, and spiritual direction can be arranged on request.

See the rooms

Group Retreats

Overnight accommodation for up to thirty retreatants, with meeting space, dining, and grounds that hold a group comfortably. Parishes, recovery fellowships, and ministries have returned here for years.

Plan a group retreat

Hosted Gatherings

Days of reflection, workshops, board retreats, and quiet celebrations. Tell us the shape of your gathering and we will help you fit it to the house, the chapel, and the grounds.

Start a conversation

The grounds

Gardens, paths, and quiet corners

The property was made for walking. Paths lead from the guest house out through the gardens and into the oaks, past benches set where the valley opens up below.

  • A granite-lined grotto for prayer and stillness
  • Stations of the Cross set along the hillside
  • A walking labyrinth open to all guests
  • Nature trails through oak and madrone
  • Gardens, benches, and long views over the valley
“We came for a weekend and left steadier than we arrived. The quiet here does most of the work.”
A returning retreat group

Where you are

Southern Oregon, just off the valley floor

We are minutes from Interstate 5 and a short drive from Medford, Jacksonville, and Ashland — close enough to reach easily, far enough that the road noise never follows you up the hill.

Guests often balance their time here with an afternoon on the Rogue River, a walk through a historic downtown, or a play in Ashland. Others never leave the grounds. Both are the right way to spend the week.

About

A steady home base

A place to gather, to return to, and to reconnect — held quietly on a hill above the Rogue River Valley.

Our story

Open since the mid-1980s

St Rita's Retreat opened in the mid-1980s on a rise of oak-covered hillside outside Gold Hill, Oregon. It was built for a single purpose, and that purpose has not changed: to give people a quiet place to step out of ordinary time for a few days.

Since then the hill has held parish weekends and silent retreats, recovery fellowships and ministry gatherings, and a great many people who simply needed somewhere to be alone with their thoughts. Many of the groups who come have been coming for decades.

The buildings have been cared for and added to over the years — new stations along the hillside, tended gardens, repaired paths — but the scale has stayed deliberately small.

What we offer

Simple comfort, without distraction

Room to be quiet

No televisions in the rooms, no crowded schedule, no reason to hurry. The house is kept quiet by common agreement, and guests are trusted to keep it that way for one another.

Space that fits the day

A chapel for prayer, a library for reading, a lounge for conversation, and meeting rooms for groups that need them — so a retreat can gather and disperse as it needs to.

Supportive hosting

Clean rooms, meals arranged in advance, and someone on hand when a question comes up. Our aim is that the practical details stay out of your way entirely.

The setting

Southern Oregon, in every direction

The valley below is known for its rivers, its mountains, and its long dry summers. The Rogue runs a few minutes from the gate. Medford, Jacksonville, and Ashland are all within easy reach, and the Oregon Shakespeare Festival draws visitors from across the country each season.

Some guests plan their retreat around the region and use the hill as a base — a morning on the water, an afternoon in a historic downtown, an evening back here where it is quiet. Others come up the drive and stay put until it is time to leave.

We have no opinion about which is better. The place works either way.

Facilities

The house and the grounds

Fifteen rooms, shared spaces that suit both silence and conversation, and a hillside made for walking.

Guest house

Fifteen rooms, up to thirty retreatants

Each room holds two single beds with a desk and chair, and opens onto either a balcony or a small patio. Every room has a private bath with a walk-in shower. Two rooms are equipped for accessibility.

Booked as singles, the house suits a group of fifteen who each want their own door to close. Shared, it accommodates thirty. Groups usually decide this with us during planning.

  • Two single beds, desk, and chair in every room
  • Private bath with walk-in shower
  • Balcony or patio off each room
  • Two rooms equipped for accessibility
  • Linens and towels provided

Shared spaces

Rooms for the whole group

Chapel

Open through the day and evening for prayer, liturgy, and silence. Groups are welcome to use it for their own scheduled services; individual guests find it quiet at almost every hour.

Library

A settled room lined with books, with chairs by the windows. Reliably the quietest space in the house and the one most guests end up claiming for an afternoon.

Lounge

Comfortable seating for conversation, small-group sessions, or an unhurried cup of coffee. It carries the social side of a retreat so the rest of the house can stay quiet.

Dining room

Seating for the full house at shared tables. Meals are arranged in advance with your group, and dietary needs can be accommodated with notice.

Meeting space

Room to present, discuss, and break out again. Tell us the format of your sessions during planning and we will set the space to match.

Spiritual direction

Available on request for guests on personal retreat and for groups who would like it offered during their stay. Please ask when you inquire so we can arrange it.

Outdoors

The grounds

The hillside is part of the retreat, not the scenery around it. Paths run from the guest house through the gardens and out into the oaks, with benches set where the valley opens below.

  • A granite-lined grotto
  • Stations of the Cross along the hillside
  • A walking labyrinth
  • Nature trails through oak and madrone
  • Gardens, benches, and open views over the Rogue River Valley

Availability & Booking

Start with an inquiry

Send your preferred dates, your group size, and what you hope the retreat will hold. We review every inquiry and reply within one to two business days.

How booking works

Three steps

  1. Send your inquiry

    Give us a date range rather than a single date if you can — it widens what we are able to offer you, especially in spring and autumn.

  2. We confirm availability

    Within one to two business days we will write back with what is open, what the house can hold for your group, and the next steps.

  3. Contract and deposit

    Your dates are held once the contract is signed and the deposit received. The contract sets out meals, capacity, and check-in and check-out times.

Choose an arrival date and a departure date below and they will carry into the form. The calendar shows what we know today; your dates are only confirmed once we reply.

Inquiry form

Request your dates

We reply to every inquiry within one to two business days. Sending this form does not hold a date; dates are held on a signed contract and deposit.

Good to know

Deposits, capacity, and cancellation

Holding your dates

Dates are confirmed once we have a signed contract and your deposit. Until then an inquiry is a conversation, not a reservation — so if your plans are firm, it is worth moving early.

Cancellation

Cancelling more than 90 days before your event refunds 50% of the deposit. Cancelling within 90 days of the event forfeits the deposit.

Capacity

Capacity depends on the type of event and how rooms are shared. Your contract states the maximum number of overnight guests and commuters for your retreat.

Check-in and check-out

Times are set in your contract so that the house can be turned over between groups. Let us know in advance if your travel makes those times difficult.

Rather talk it through?

Call 541-660-0032 and we can usually tell you in a few minutes whether your dates will work.

Finding us

Off Blackwell Road, above the valley

Medford Airport is roughly twenty-five minutes away. Groups arriving together are welcome to ask about parking when they book.
